title: Coordinate quotients factor through the dual kernel
statement: Let K be a field, V and W K-vector spaces, A a commutative K-algebra, E:V -> W linear, and H:Sym_K(V*) -> A a surjective algebra homomorphism. If H kills the degree-one elements E*(phi) for every phi in W*, then there is a surjective algebra homomorphism G:Sym_K((ker E)*) -> A whose value on every restricted ambient functional agrees with H on that functional. Symmetric algebras have their usual universal property; no finite-dimensionality or surjectivity of E is required.

source.place: Tag 0FD6, lemma-bertini, final paragraph: first-order evaluation and its kernel

proof.text: Restriction V* -> (ker E)* has a linear section Subspace.dualLift. Its kernel is the annihilator of ker E, equal to the range of E.dualMap by LinearMap.range_dualMap_eq_dualAnnihilator_ker. Thus the linear part t of H kills this kernel. Compose t with that section to get l. The difference phi-dualLift(restriction(phi)) is annihilating, so l(restriction(phi))=t(phi).

Use SymmetricAlgebra.lift l to get G. The symmetric-algebra map R induced by restriction satisfies G.comp R=H by algHom_ext and equality on degree-one generators. Every element of A is H(b)=G(R(b)), so G is surjective. The generator equation is lift_ι_apply.

lean.statement:
theorem symmetricAlgebra_factor_through_dual_kernel
    {K : Type u} [Field K]
    {V : Type v} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V]
    {W : Type w} [AddCommGroup W] [Module K W]
    {A : Type x} [CommRing A] [Algebra K A]
    (E : V →ₗ[K] W) (H : SymmetricAlgebra K (Dual K V) →ₐ[K] A)
    (hH : Function.Surjective H)
    (hzero : ∀ φ : Dual K W, H (SymmetricAlgebra.ι K (Dual K V) (E.dualMap φ)) = 0) :
    ∃ G : SymmetricAlgebra K (Dual K E.ker) →ₐ[K] A,
      Function.Surjective G ∧
      ∀ φ : Dual K V,
        G (SymmetricAlgebra.ι K (Dual K E.ker) (E.ker.dualRestrict φ)) =
          H (SymmetricAlgebra.ι K (Dual K V) φ)
